chief_complaint: morning stiffness and pain in my hands
hpi_details: 35F presents with a 4-month history of pain, swelling, and stiffness in the small joints of both hands (MCPs and PIPs). The stiffness is worst in the morning and lasts for 2 hours.
concerns: worried her hands will become deformed

core_concepts: Symmetric polyarthritis involving small joints (MCP, PIP, sparing DIP).
common_misconceptions: Assuming osteoarthritis (which affects DIPs and has brief morning stiffness).
dangerous_errors: Delaying DMARD therapy, leading to irreversible joint destruction.
management_principles: Prompt rheumatology referral for clinician-directed DMARD therapy; methotrexate or a steroid bridge require pregnancy, infection, liver/kidney function, interaction, and monitoring review. NSAIDs require gastrointestinal, renal, cardiovascular, and anticoagulant-risk assessment.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Clinical Guidance

reference_soap.subjective: 35F with symmetric pain and swelling in hand joints and 2-hour morning stiffness.
reference_soap.objective: Bilateral MCP and PIP synovitis (swelling, warmth, tenderness). DIPs spared.
reference_soap.plan: Order RF, anti-CCP, ESR/CRP, CBC, renal/liver function, and hand radiographs; refer promptly to rheumatology for individualized DMARD planning. Screen pregnancy plans, infection risk, comorbidities, and medication interactions before immunosuppression; urgently assess an acutely hot joint with fever for septic arthritis.

learning_objectives: Differentiate RA from osteoarthritis based on joint pattern and morning stiffness.

teaching.one_liner: Symmetric polyarthritis of the small hand joints with prolonged morning stiffness in a young female.
red_flags: An acutely hot, severely painful joint with fever or systemic illness may be septic arthritis and needs urgent assessment.
New neurologic symptoms or neck pain after trauma in established RA warrants urgent assessment for cervical spine involvement.

must_ask.say: Are both hands affected in the same joints on each side?
How long does the stiffness in your hands last after you wake up?
How many months has this been going on, and is it getting worse?
Have you felt unusually tired, or had any low-grade fevers?
Is the stiffness making it hard to grip things or get dressed?
